set_title: Hot-and-rigid drug reactions: NMS vs serotonin syndrome vs malignant hyperthermia vs anticholinergic
stem: A 40-year-old woman taking sertraline was started on tramadol 2 days ago. She now has agitation, sweating, diarrhea and temperature 38.8 C. Examination shows inducible ankle clonus and brisk reflexes.
oneliner: 40-year-old woman, SSRI plus tramadol, diarrhea, clonus, hyperreflexia → ?

whyNot.B: Slow onset with lead-pipe rigidity and normal reflexes; she has **clonus and diarrhea**
whyNot.C: Follows volatile anesthetic exposure; she has **SSRI plus tramadol, clonus and diarrhea**
whyNot.D: Dry skin and absent bowel sounds; she has **sweating and diarrhea**
whyNot.E: Follows heat exposure without clonus; she has **an SSRI-tramadol combination**

why: Too much serotonin overstimulates 5-HT receptors. **A new serotonergic drug with clonus, hyperreflexia and diarrhea** gives it away.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Hot, dry, red, blind, mad; no sweating**
**Over 40 C with CNS dysfunction after heat**

idea.rule: Clonus and diarrhea = serotonin; lead-pipe rigidity = NMS; dry skin = anticholinergic.
also: Onset within hours; treat with cyproheptadine

set_title: Hot-and-rigid drug reactions: NMS vs serotonin syndrome vs malignant hyperthermia vs anticholinergic
stem: A 20-year-old man has a laparoscopic appendectomy under halothane and succinylcholine. Thirty minutes in, end-tidal CO2 rises to 70 mm Hg, temperature reaches 40.5 C, and his jaw and limbs become rigid.
oneliner: 20-year-old man, halothane and succinylcholine, rising CO2, rigidity, high temperature → ?

whyNot.A: Needs days of antipsychotic therapy; his rigidity began **under anesthesia**
whyNot.B: Needs a serotonergic drug with clonus; his reaction began **under halothane and succinylcholine**
whyNot.C: Causes dry skin and dilated pupils; he has **rigidity and rising CO2 under anesthesia**
whyNot.E: Follows heat exposure; his temperature rose **30 minutes into anesthesia**

why: Malignant (life-threatening) hyperthermia: RYR1 defect lets halothane or succinylcholine trigger calcium release. **Rising CO2, rigidity and fever under anesthesia** is classic.

idea.rule: Anesthetic trigger plus rising CO2 and rigidity = MH; treat with dantrolene.

set_title: Hot-and-rigid drug reactions: NMS vs serotonin syndrome vs malignant hyperthermia vs anticholinergic
stem: An 8-year-old boy is brought in after eating seeds from a roadside plant. He is agitated and hallucinating, with flushed dry skin, dilated pupils, temperature 38.3 C, absent bowel sounds and urinary retention.
oneliner: 8-year-old boy, ate seeds from a plant, hot dry flushed skin, dilated pupils, retention → ?

whyNot.A: Causes rigidity, not dry skin; he has **dilated pupils and absent bowel sounds**
whyNot.B: Causes sweating, diarrhea and clonus; he has **dry skin and absent bowel sounds**
whyNot.D: Follows anesthetic exposure; he has **flushed dry skin after eating seeds**
whyNot.E: Follows heat exposure; he has **dilated pupils and urinary retention**

why: Anti- (against) + cholinergic: muscarinic blockade, so dry, red, hot, dilated and mad. **Dry flushed skin, dilated pupils, retention and agitation** fit.

idea.rule: Anticholinergic = dry skin; serotonin and NMS = sweating or rigidity.

set_title: Hot-and-rigid drug reactions: NMS vs serotonin syndrome vs malignant hyperthermia vs anticholinergic
stem: A 30-year-old man started haloperidol 5 days ago. He now has temperature 40 C, marked generalized lead-pipe rigidity, confusion, and creatine kinase 12,000 U/L. Reflexes are normal and there is no clonus.
oneliner: 30-year-old man, haloperidol, fever, lead-pipe rigidity, high CK, no clonus → ?

whyNot.B: Causes clonus and hyperreflexia; he has **lead-pipe rigidity with normal reflexes**
whyNot.C: Needs anesthetic exposure; his fever followed **days of haloperidol**
whyNot.D: Causes dry skin and dilated pupils; he has **rigidity and CK 12,000 U/L**
whyNot.E: Follows heat exposure; he has **lead-pipe rigidity after haloperidol**

why: Neuroleptic (antipsychotic) + malignant (life-threatening) syndrome: dopamine blockade. **Haloperidol, lead-pipe rigidity, fever and high CK** are classic.

idea.rule: NMS = slow onset, lead-pipe rigidity, normal reflexes; serotonin syndrome = rapid, clonus.
also: Dopamine D2 blockade; treat with dantrolene

set_title: Antipsychotic movement names: acute dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia
stem: A 65-year-old man has taken risperidone for 3 months. He now has a shuffling gait, a mask-like face and a pill-rolling tremor at rest. Muscle tone is increased in cogwheel pattern in both arms. He has no fever, and CK is normal.
oneliner: 65M, risperidone 3 months + shuffling gait, masked face, rest tremor, cogwheel rigidity both arms → ?

whyNot.A: Tardive dyskinesia gives orofacial movements; he has **tremor and cogwheel rigidity**
whyNot.B: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome has fever and high CK; he has **normal temperature and CK**
whyNot.C: Akathisia is restlessness; he has **slow movements and rigidity**
whyNot.E: Acute dystonia is sudden spasm; his signs developed **over 3 months**

why: Dopamine blockade in the striatum mimics Parkinson disease: **bilateral rigidity, bradykinesia and tremor** weeks to months after starting the drug.

idea.rule: Drug-induced parkinsonism = symmetric, weeks, reversible; treat with benztropine.
